title: Balogun Scored. Then He Was Sent Off. Ten-Man USA Beat Bosnia 2-0 in the Bay Area to Reach the World Cup Round of 16.
excerpt: Folarin Balogun’s third goal of the tournament and a stunning Malik Tillman free kick powered the Americans past Bosnia at Levi’s Stadium — ending a 24-year wait for a knockout-stage win, with NRIs in Silicon Valley celebrating alongside them.
body:
The World Cup came to Silicon Valley on Wednesday night, and the United States sent it home with a statement.

Folarin Balogun fired the Americans ahead just before halftime, Malik Tillman curled in a free kick masterpiece in the 82nd minute, and the USMNT held off Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara — playing more than half an hour with ten men after Balogun’s controversial red card.

It is the United States’ first knockout-stage win at a World Cup since beating Mexico in 2002. For the nearly 69,000 supporters packed into the Bay Area’s most famous stadium, and for the millions watching across the country, it felt like the beginning of something bigger.

## Balogun Opens the Scoring — Then Exits

The first half belonged to Balogun. The Monaco striker terrorized the Bosnian backline from the opening whistle, had a goal chalked off for offside, and finally broke through in the 45th minute. A Malik Tillman through ball took a deflection and fell into Balogun’s path. He turned, sorted his feet, and fired through the legs of goalkeeper Nikola Vasilj.

It was Balogun’s third goal of the tournament, confirming him as one of the breakout stars of the 2026 World Cup.


![Bay Area — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/OAKLAND%2C_CA%2C_USA_-_Skyline_and_Bridge.JPG/3840px-OAKLAND%2C_CA%2C_USA_-_Skyline_and_Bridge.JPG)


But his evening took a dramatic turn in the 64th minute. After a tangle of legs with Bosnia’s centre-back Tarik Muharemović, Balogun’s studs came down on the defender’s ankle. The referee initially let play continue, but after a VAR review, a straight red card was produced. Balogun walked off in disbelief, the challenge looking more accidental than malicious.

The ejection means he will be suspended for the Round of 16 — a significant blow.

## Tillman’s Free Kick Seals It



> **"For the nearly 69,000 supporters packed into the Bay Area’s most famous stadium, and for the millions watching across the country, it felt like the beginning of something bigger."**


Down to ten men, the USA retreated into a low block for the first time all tournament. Bosnia finally found urgency, pressing forward with increasing desperation. For twenty tense minutes, the Americans bent but didn’t break.

Then Malik Tillman stepped up and ended the argument.

In the 82nd minute, he stood over a free kick just outside the Bosnia box, lifted it up and over the wall, and watched it curl past Vasilj’s fingertips and into the net. Levi’s Stadium erupted. It was a goal worthy of winning any match — and it gave ten-man USA the breathing room they desperately needed.


![Silicon Valley — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Silicon_Valley%2C_facing_southward_towards_Downtown_San_Jose%2C_2014_%28cropped%29.jpg/3840px-Silicon_Valley%2C_facing_southward_towards_Downtown_San_Jose%2C_2014_%28cropped%29.jpg)


Even with ten minutes of stoppage time added, Bosnia never seriously threatened. The final whistle triggered “U-S-A! U-S-A!” chants that echoed across the Santa Clara evening.

## A 24-Year Wait, Over

The last time the United States won a World Cup knockout match, it was June 2002 in Suwon, South Korea. Landon Donovan and Brian McBride led the Americans past Mexico 2-0 in the Round of 16. The country had been waiting ever since — through a group-stage exit in 2006, a painful Round of 16 loss to Belgium in 2014, and the humiliation of failing to qualify in 2018.

Wednesday’s win also snapped a 10-game losing streak against European teams in World Cup play. The Americans hadn’t beaten a European side at the tournament since defeating Portugal in the 2002 group stage — a drought spanning 13 consecutive matches.

The historic significance was not lost on the crowd, many of whom had traveled from across the Bay Area and beyond. The game was played less than 20 miles from Stanford Stadium, where the US lost 1-0 to Brazil in the 1994 World Cup’s Round of 16. Thirty-two years later, on nearly the same patch of California soil, the story finally had a different ending.

## The Bay Area’s World Cup Moment


![Malik Tillman — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/68/Malik_Tillman_Australia_v_USA_19_June_2026-66.jpg)


For Indian Americans in Silicon Valley — and across the Bay Area — Wednesday night was something altogether new. This is a community that grew up on cricket, on IPL matches streamed at odd hours, on Sachin and Kohli and Dhoni. Football was always the sport they watched from the outside.

But a World Cup at your doorstep changes that calculus. Traffic on the 101 was redirected around Levi’s Stadium hours before kickoff. Watch parties filled bars from San Jose to San Francisco. Indian-American families with American flags and face paint filled sections of the upper deck.

For NRIs who have made the Bay Area home — who have built careers, started families, planted roots in Sunnyvale and Cupertino and Fremont — this was a chance to be part of something that doesn’t come around often. The World Cup, in their neighborhood, with the country they now call their own fighting for its sporting life.

The atmosphere delivered. And the team matched it.

## What’s Next

The United States advances to face Belgium in the Round of 16 on Monday, July 6, at Lumen Field in Seattle — another city with a large and passionate South Asian diaspora. Belgium arrived the hard way, rallying from 2-0 down to beat Senegal 3-2 in extra time earlier on Wednesday in Seattle.

The bad news for the USMNT: they will be without Balogun, their most dangerous attacker. Head coach Gregg Berhalter will need to reconfigure his forward line, likely turning to Ricardo Pepi — who came on as a substitute against Bosnia — or redeploying Christian Pulisic in a more central role.

The good news: what this team showed on Wednesday — the grit to defend with ten men, the composure to create a match-sealing goal under pressure, the refusal to concede — is exactly what knockout football demands.

Twenty-four years is a long time to wait. Now the Americans want more.

*Sources: Reuters, USA Today, NBC Sports Bay Area, Fox Sports*
